name: Alfa Romeo
overview: The passionate Italian driver's marque, renowned in Australia for melodic twin-cam engines, Bathurst class victories, and the Giorgio-platform Giulia and Stelvio.
australian_history: Alfa Romeo established strong Australian presence in the 1960s with distributor Alec Mildren, whose racing team campaigned Giulia and GTA models with immense success. At the Bathurst 500, Alfa Romeo GT and 1750 GTVs won their classes repeatedly. The 105 Series Giulia, Bertone Coupe (1750/2000 GTV), and Spider Veloce became Australian motoring royalty. Transaxle models like the Alfetta, GTV6, and 75 followed in the 1970s and 1980s. Modern Alfa Romeo is represented by the 156, 147, 159, and the celebrated rear-wheel-drive Giorgio platform: the Giulia sports sedan and Stelvio SUV, crowned by 375kW Ferrari-developed 2.9L twin-turbo V6 Quadrifoglio models.

models_catalog.name: Giulia
models_catalog.overview: The quintessential sports sedan across classic 105 series and modern Giorgio-platform Type 952 with 50:50 weight balance.

generations.summary: Giulia TI, Super, and Nuova Super with all-alloy DOHC twin-cam 1.3L and 1.6L and 5-speed manual.
Carbon-fibre driveshaft, 2.0L Turbo (147kW/206kW Veloce), and 375kW 2.9L Twin-Turbo V6 Quadrifoglio.

models_catalog.name: 105 GTV / Spider
models_catalog.overview: Bertone-designed Giulia Sprint GT, 1750 GTV, and Pininfarina Spider; revered collector cars in Australia.

generations.summary: Sprint GT, GT Veloce, 1750 GTV, and 2000 GTV with limited-slip differential and 4-wheel disc brakes.
Osso di seppia 'boat tail' Duetto through Kamm-tail Spider 2000 Veloce.

models_catalog.name: Stelvio
models_catalog.overview: Alfa Romeo's first production SUV, sharing the Giorgio architecture and steering sharpness of the Giulia.

generations.summary: Q4 all-wheel drive, 2.0T (147kW/206kW Veloce), and 375kW Quadrifoglio with torque-vectoring rear diff.

models_catalog.name: Giulia Sprint GT, GTV & Giulia Quadrifoglio
models_catalog.overview: The passionate soul of Italian motoring in Australia. Spanning from the Bertone-styled 105 Series Giulia Sprint GT and Bathurst-winning 1750/2000 GTV, through the transaxle Alfetta GTV6 Group A touring car, to the spine-tingling Busso V6 156 GTA and the modern Giorgio-platform Giulia Quadrifoglio with its Ferrari-derived 375kW twin-turbo V6.

generations.summary: Masterpiece designed by Giorgetto Giugiaro for Bertone. Featured all-alloy twin-cam four-cylinder engines, twin Weber/Dell'Orto carburettors, 5-speed manual, four-wheel disc brakes, and Bathurst 500 class dominance.

Innovative 50:50 weight distribution chassis featuring a rear-mounted transaxle gearbox/clutch, inboard rear disc brakes, De Dion rear axle, 2.0L twin-cam, and the glorious 2.5L Busso V6 GTV6 raced in the ATCC by Colin Bond.

Built on the clean-sheet Giorgio rear-wheel-drive platform with 50:50 weight distribution and carbon-fibre driveshaft. Features the 206kW Veloce and the halo Quadrifoglio powered by a 375kW 2.9L 90-degree twin-turbo V6 developed in collaboration with Ferrari engineers.
